path.what: a confirmed place for the task instead of searching the web and judging what comes back
path.basis: An agent that searches does about 3 to 7 model turns (search, read, judge). A web task of the simplest level in the GAIA benchmark took about 26,000 input and 4,700 output tokens; the place someone already found spares the searching part of it. Energy: 3 turns at 0.16 Wh up to 7 turns at 0.60 Wh, 5 at the median 0.31 Wh.

plan.what: a worked-out method with steps, checks and a quality bar instead of working it out again
plan.basis: Working out a method is reasoning: a long reasoning query writes about 5,000 output tokens and uses 3.91 Wh at the median. Low: one ordinary query (0.31 Wh). Mid: 40 % of a reasoning query.

market.what: stores that passed open checks instead of checking unknown shops one by one
market.basis: Checking a shop means reading its home and legal pages, its registration and what others say: about 2 to 4 reads of 5,000 to 15,000 tokens for each of 2 or 3 shops, and the judgement. Energy: 3 to 15 ordinary queries.

sources.what: Energy of one query to a frontier model: median 0.31 Wh (0.16–0.60); a long reasoning query (test-time scaling, about 5,000 output tokens) 3.91 Wh (2.15–7.05)
Tokens of one agent task: about 26,000 input and 4,700 output at the easiest GAIA level, 121,000 and 9,800 at the hardest
Agents use about 4 times the tokens of a chat, systems of several agents about 15 times
Data centres used about 415 TWh in 2024, about 1.5 % of the world's electricity, heading for about 945 TWh by 2030
Data centres used about 485 TWh in 2025, heading for about 950 TWh in 2030

notCounted: the energy of the sea itself (one small server; a lookup is milliseconds of one processor, far below one model query)

ratio.basis: measured, not assumed: on the 33 pages of the proof of function (2026-11-24, tokenizer o200k_base) one token held 3.22 characters of raw HTML (3.23 UTF-8 bytes), 3.58 of the sea's Markdown (3.59) and 4.32 of plain text (4.34). Each count becomes tokens with the ratio of its form and of the unit it was counted in: UTF-8 bytes for pages of the sea, characters for pages read through the reader and for counts from before 3.33.0

source.what: Characters and UTF-8 bytes per token for raw HTML, plain text and the sea's Markdown, counted with the o200k_base tokenizer on the 33 pages of a published task set

read: A reuse counts once a day per caller network and task when an answer handed an agent a part someone already solved: a confirmed pathway (path), a ready plan (plan), verified offers (market); what it spares is modelled from the ranges in perReuse (low, mid, high). Markdown is measured: md counts pages of the sea asked for as Markdown, mdAgent pages of the sea sent as Markdown to an assistant reading for a person (md-agent), reads pages of other sites through the reader, each with what it spared against the page as HTML (UTF-8 bytes for pages of the sea, characters for pages through the reader); counts become tokens by one rule (ratio: HTML 3.23 bytes or 3.22 characters a token, Markdown 3.59 bytes or 3.58 characters, measured with o200k_base on the proof of function (https://mareliberum.dev/proof)). usd prices the tokens at list prices for uncached input tokens (price): low, mid (the headline) and high. A Markdown answer counts once a day per network and page; one network adds at most 500 Markdown answers and 500 reuses a day. measured is against raw HTML, an upper bound; vsText is the same answers against plain text (pages of the sea), the lower view. The sea's own calls and crawlers are never counted; the house agent (Angel) is counted apart (house).
